Company Description
✨ About Voyage Privé
Born in France in 2006, Voyage Privé has grown from an ambitious startup into becoming Europe’s leading travel tech platform. Operating across 9 markets with tens of millions of users, we're not just another e-commerce success story — we're a tech powerhouse revolutionizing online travel.
What makes us unique? A mission-driven culture where performance meets impact. Our innovative campus brings together tech talent, professional athletes, students, and artists, creating an ecosystem where digital innovation drives both business growth and positive change.
We have reached this scale by staying fully independent, fully profitable, and achieving double-digit growth.
We're now at an inflection point, upgrading our entire technical foundation with cloud architecture, AI, and real-time systems to become a global reference for luxury travel — known by travelers for its excellent offer and customer experience, and by our providers as a high-performance business development partner.
Job Description

As a Software Engineer, you are a product-driven builder embedded in on of our four domains alongside Product Managers, Designers, Data and Business stakeholders.
You design, build and operate software systems that power high-traffic, business-critical travel experiences.
You don’t just ship features — you own systems end to end and contribute directly to measurable business and customer impact.

Build high-impact solutions
Develop, test and deploy reliable, scalable software in a high-traffic environment, embedding AI-first capabilities
Break down complex problems into pragmatic solutions that deliver value fast
Continuously improve performance, maintainability and system reliability
Own systems end to end
Take responsibility for design, implementation, deployment and production operations
Participate in on-call rotations and incident resolution
Proactively identify technical debt and improvement opportunities
Ensure systems are observable, resilient and ready to scale
Design robust and scalable architectures
Contribute to architecture decisions with a strong understanding of trade-offs (performance, cost, scalability, security)
Design APIs and services that integrate smoothly within a complex travel ecosystem
Apply security-by-design principles to protect customers and business operations
Work with a strong product & data mindset
Collaborate closely with Product Managers to align technical decisions with business goals
Use data and feedback to validate impact and guide improvements
Enable experimentation, iteration and continuous learning
Contribute to engineering excellence
Uphold high standards in code quality, testing and documentation
Actively participate in code reviews and knowledge sharing
Help evolve engineering practices, tooling and team maturity
We’re looking for engineers who think in systems, care about impact, and take ownership beyond their code.

Strong software engineering fundamentals in at least one modern programming language
Experience building and operating production systems
Solid understanding of APIs, distributed systems and integrations
Awareness of performance, scalability and security best practices
Comfortable with testing, version control and CI/CD practices
Product-oriented mindset and ability to translate business needs into technical solutions
Strong ownership, autonomy and collaboration skills
Good communication in English and French
Additional Information
⚡ Our Recruitment Process
We believe in a fast, transparent, and human recruitment process.

Intro Call with a Talent Acquisition Partner (30/45 min) – Get to know each other! We’ll share more about the role, the team, and our culture.
Live Coding (60min)

Final Interview (60 min) – Meet with the Hiring Manager and/or leadership team to align on expectations, culture, and long-term impact.
Location : Aix en Provence, France or remote
Start Date : The sooner, the better
Contract Type : Full-time / Permanent
❤️ You'll Love Joining Us
Our HQ in the South of France offers an exceptional environment — natural, cultural, and digital — on a modern and eco-responsible campus.
Prefer flexibility? We offer full remote work for selected Digital roles, and a hybrid model for all other positions with 3 mandatory on-site days per week plus 4 fully remote weeks per year.
Put meaning back into your work and join a unique ecosystem that connects worlds often far apart: business, sports, education, and social impact — through projects like Ecole des XV, Provence Rugby, VP Green, Les Tremplins, and Chez Pierre.
Forget your gym subscription! Access our large on-site fitness center morning, noon, and night — or challenge your colleagues to a padel match on our private court.
Live to the rhythm of Voyage Privé’s signature mix of business and fun: Company Breaks, Carnival, Annual Convention, meetups and talks… plus free tickets to every Provence Rugby home match and live music nights at the Dalida Institute .
✈️ And because travel is in our DNA : enjoy up to 20% off our exclusive getaway offers.
Join us and make your next career move a journey worth taking.

About Variant Security
Variant Security is securing the world's critical fleets for the AI era. Today nearly every device runs identical software, so a single exploit can cascade across an entire fleet of satellites, drones, vehicles, and defense systems, and AI has made finding that one exploit cheaper than ever.

Variant breaks that pattern, so compromising one device gives an attacker nothing against the rest and no single failure can bring down the fleet. AI made exploits cheap, and we make them useless, already protecting systems across aerospace, defense, and active conflict zones.

As a Compiler Engineer, you'll build and own the compiler technology at the core of Variant's product, turning cutting-edge diversification into something that ships. You'll work across two areas, the compiler itself and the systems and tooling that run it at fleet scale, with real ownership rather than narrow ticket work.

You'll have a direct line to the founding team, immediate impact on what customers run, and room to grow from a strong early-career engineer into the owner of a core domain. Variant Security is securing the world's critical fleets for the AI era.

Tasks
Develop and extend compiler passes that harden builds against exploitation
Reverse engineer and analyze the generated binaries to validate transformations
Measure security and performance impact across x86, AArch64, and RISC-V targets
Build tooling in modern C++ and Python, and integrate the compiler into CMake and customer CI/CD

Master's degree, or equivalent hands-on experience, in cybersecurity or computer science
Hands-on experience with binaries, whether reverse engineering, exploitation, or vulnerability research
Familiarity with Python and modern C++
Comfortable reading assembly and debugging low-level code on at least one of x86, AArch64, or RISC-V
Self-organized and self-driven, with strong personal initiative

Prior work on compilers like Clang/LLVM or IR-level transformations
Familiarity with binary analysis tooling such as Ghidra, IDA, or Binary Ninja
Knowledge of exploit mitigations (ASLR, CFI, stack canaries, DEP)
CTF, pwn, or fuzzing experience (AFL, libFuzzer)
Low-level systems background, spanning embedded, firmware, OS internals, or ELF/PE formats, linkers, and loaders

Work on rare, hard problems where compilers meet binary security, the kind most engineers never get to touch
Early-stage equity and competitive compensation on the ground floor
Learn directly from a founding team with deep security, compiler, and space-systems pedigree (top-tier security research, DARPA, SpaceX)
See your work protect real fleets across aerospace, defense, and active conflict zones
Based in the Bochum office, with regular collaboration across Germany and the U.S. and the chance to work from or visit the US team

The IPAOT team at NBCUniversal is looking for a self-motivated, highly organized, proactive, and passionate problem solver who will assist with the design, build, and ongoing maintenance of content and rights management systems, as well as content delivery systems and pipelines.

We're looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer to sit between our platform and the people who use it, quickly turning what our team and our clients actually need into working software.
Who we are 👪
We believe live music is one of the best things humans do, and that far more artists deserve to make a living from it than currently can. That's the opportunity we're building for.
The industry still runs on cold emails and who-knows-who, and it's about to be rebuilt. AI now lets small teams achieve incredible things, and we intend to be the team that rebuilds this one.
Otherworldly is an AI-native talent management and booking company. We run an actual roster, meaning real tours, real riders, real settlements, and we're turning everything we've learned into agentic infrastructure. That means a database of 250,000+ bookers worldwide and algorithmic pitching systems that get the right artist in front of the right promoter at scale.
It's working. We closed our seed round with roster and revenue traction already built. Between us, we've managed No.1 artists and Grammy nominees, led strategy for household-name brands, and founded YC-backed companies. Most music-tech is built by people who've never booked a show, but we book shows every week.
Tasks
Most companies keep their engineers away from customers.
We do the opposite.
Our team runs real tours, pitches real promoters, and manages real artists every day, and every one of those workflows is a system waiting to be built. Your job is to live at that boundary. That means watching the work happen, finding the friction, and shipping the feature that removes it.

· Embed with the booking and artist-care teams. Sit with them, watch how they actually work, and turn the messiest, most manual parts of their day into software

· Build and ship end-to-end. You'll take a problem from "the team keeps doing this by hand" to a deployed, working feature, often in days, not sprints

· Own the last mile of the agentic platform. The integrations, workflows, and interfaces that decide whether our AI systems actually provide value

· Close the loop between roster and product. You're the person who hears an artist's or booker's real problem and comes back with a solution, then feeds what you learn back into the core platform

· Be the technical face to our users when it counts. You're comfortable in the room with a manager, a promoter, or an artist, not just behind a screen

You'll thrive here if...
🚢 You ship fast and talk to users. You're comfortable reading a spec or sitting with the person who has the problem. You prototype, iterate, and get something working fast.
🛠 You're a generalist who finishes things. Frontend, backend, glue code, an LLM call, a scrappy integration, you'll do whatever the problem needs, and you take it all the way to deployed and used
📈 You hold yourself to a high bar. You've shown ambition and excellence somewhere in your life - professionally, academically, or otherwise, and you want your work to matter
🎵 You love music, or want to work for people who do. Everything we build exists to get artists booked, paid, and heard.

· Strong full-stack engineering experience. You can build and ship a working product feature end-to-end, from data to interface, without waiting on anyone

· Comfort integrating LLMs into real products. You feel comfortable with API calls, prompt design, structured outputs, and knowing when the model is the wrong tool

· A track record of shipping fast in ambiguous, early-stage environments. Be that startups, founding teams, or your own projects

· Excellent communication and a genuine willingness to spend time with non-technical users, understand their work, and earn their trust

· Solid Python and/or JavaScript/TypeScript, and the pragmatism to pick up whatever the job needs
Strong plus ✅

· Experience as a forward deployed / solutions / founding engineer, or any role where you owned the boundary between product and customer

· Familiarity with agentic frameworks and the LLM stack (embeddings, vector DBs, RAG, evaluation)

· Background building internal tools, workflow automation, or CRM/outbound systems
· A real connection to the music industry or its tools

· Early-stage equity and genuine ownership of the core agentic architecture

· Direct influence on the product roadmap from day one

· A front-row seat to an industry being rebuilt, working from Berlin, one of the world's great music cities

· Access to one of the most exciting sectors on earth, working with musicians, venues, brands, and talent agents.

Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases.

The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.
The Simulation ML Infrastructure team builds scalable AI/ML infrastructure to accelerate the Simulator team in sustainably innovating and building state of the art simulations of realistic environments for the testing and training of the Waymo Driver.

To increase the fidelity and steerability of the simulations, we employ large foundation models trained on massive datasets to model the real world, including but not limited to, realistic agents (vehicles, pedestrians, cyclists, motorcyclists etc.), roads, traffic control systems, and weather etc.
We seek an experienced Senior Machine Learning Infrastructure Engineer to lead the development of advanced AI/ML infrastructure for multi-billion parameter foundation models in ML accelerator-friendly simulations. Collaborate closely with the core Google DeepMind and Waymo Realism Modeling teams in London, and Waymo Oxford to use the large models to improve sim realism.
Provide deep technical leadership on large-scale ML model architectures, especially for autonomous vehicle models. Design and scale large distributed systems covering the ML lifecycle, supporting planet-scale dataset generation and model training.
Collaborate cross-functionally to derive performance and system-level requirements for large ML systems. Translate product/business goals into measurable technical deliverables, ensuring system component alignment.
Mentor junior engineers, growing their expertise and fostering a collaborative culture.

MS in Computer Science, Robotics, similar technical field of study, or equivalent practical experience

Solid experience in the development and optimization of machine learning infrastructure tools like DeepSpeed, PyTorch, TensorFlow, or similar frameworks.

Join us as a (Senior) Backend Software Engineer (all genders) in our Vehicle Perception team and help shape the future of autonomous mobility!
To realise the vision of autonomous ride pooling, the Vehicle Integration domain develops the tools and applications that make passenger management possible without a driver. How can passengers authenticate themselves in the vehicle? How do we ensure a safe cabin during boarding and the ride? What content should be shown on the screens to create a safe and informative experience?
The Vehicle Perception team addresses some of these challenges by building end-to-end solutions for live video streaming, operator communication, and computer vision inside our vehicles. The team develops the technical foundation for real-time cabin awareness.

This includes live video pipelines that stream reliably from the vehicle to backend systems, as well as interfaces and services that enable operators to connect with passengers and provide timely support.

In addition, it implements perception models that are meant to detect and classify cabin states — for example, identifying occupied seats, forgotten objects, or compliance with safety requirements.
Our team has the necessary roles on board to take full responsibility for the given value streams: from backend and embedded developers to quality specialists, functional safety experts and product managers.
We are looking forward to getting to know you, and would be really happy to welcome you as part of our team.

At GWI we’re always looking for extraordinary people who thrive on making an extraordinary impact. Right now we’re looking for an Forward Deployed Engineer to play a key role in our Solutions Consultants Team in London. If that’s you, and making a difference gets you out of bed in the morning, keep reading. It could be the start of something, well, extraordinary.
Sounds great, what will I be doing? 🤔
As our Lead / Principal Forward Deployed Engineer you'll be embedded directly with our most strategic accounts, owning the end-to-end technical deployment of our agentic AI platform. This isn't a support role, and it isn't a solutions consultant with a fancy title — you'll write production code, own technical outcomes, and be the reason our biggest customers succeed and expand. You'll operate with the autonomy of a founding engineer and the commercial instinct of a GTM leader.

s.h: A few things you'll be responsible for
s.t:
👉 Embed with our Tier 1 enterprise accounts and own end-to-end deployments of our agentic AI platform — from discovery through to production, including bespoke integrations, data pipelines, and workflow automations.
👉 Lead AI agents into production in complex environments (legacy systems, security, compliance), turning cutting-edge capability into measurable business outcomes.
👉 Partner with Enterprise AEs in late-stage sales cycles — leading proof-of-concept builds and assessing technical readiness to de-risk and accelerate the close.
👉 Surface patterns from the field and feed them back to product and engineering, acting as the bridge between customer reality and roadmap.
👉 Build out the FDE practice as it scales: repeatable deployment playbooks, success metrics, and mentoring mid-level FDEs.
It's also fun; shaking things up is what working for GWI is all about. You'll need to be flexible, comfortable with continuous change, and working in a high-tempo environment.
What do I need to bring with me? 🧳
You’ll need to be able to demonstrate the core skills this role requires. You don't have to tick all the boxes right away; the important thing is that you’re willing to learn.

s.h: Here’s what the team will be looking for in you
s.t:
👉 Significant experience in software engineering, solutions engineering, or a customer-facing technical role — with meaningful time spent shipping production code in complex enterprise environments.
👉 Demonstrable experience deploying AI or data-heavy products into large organisations — real production deployments, not just POCs.
👉 Strong full-stack or backend engineering fundamentals: Python essential, plus comfort across APIs, SQL, cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP/Azure), and data pipelines.
👉 The ability to work through ambiguity and turn it into a concrete technical plan.
👉 Clear communication across technical and business audiences — you can tailor the same idea for an engineering lead and a commercial stakeholder.
👉 Willingness to travel to client sites across the UK and Europe (approximately 30–50% of the time).

👉 Hands-on experience with LLM deployment, AI agents, or agentic workflow automation.
👉 A background in a high-growth B2B SaaS or AI-native company.
👉 Experience in one or more of GWI's core verticals: financial services, media & agencies, consumer goods, or technology.
👉 Prior experience in an FDE, solutions architect, or technical account management function at a company with a named-account enterprise motion.
Equally important is attitude. We want people who think big (to make an impact), ask why (to find a better way), and show respect (to everyone, at every level, all the time). Those are our values, and they’re a big part of what we’re looking for in you.
What’s in it for me? 🎁
At GWI, you’ll find meaningful work, visible impact, and a culture that empowers you to do your best. Our package includes:
🌴 Time to recharge – 25 days’ annual leave, plus office closures over the holidays.
🧘 Health & wellbeing – Health cash plan, enhanced family benefits, carer days, and mental health support.
💸 Financial benefits – Competitive salary, 4% pension matching, and recognition programs that celebrate success.
🏡 Flexibility & balance – Flexitime, early Friday finishes, hybrid and remote options, plus a “work from home” budget.
💪 Career growth – Accredited learning, leadership development, and global career mobility.
🌎 Community & impact – DE&I initiatives, volunteering opportunities, donation matching, and payroll giving.
Put all that together and GWI is the friendliest, most fulfilling place any of us has ever worked.
Diversity, Equity & Inclusion
Diversity is fundamental to who we are—both as a data company and as a workplace. Our data reflects global realities, and so must our teams. We strive to ensure our workforce is as diverse and inclusive as the insights we provide to our clients.
As a Disability Confident employer, we welcome applications from disabled candidates and are committed to providing all necessary adjustments during the hiring process. We also actively encourage applications from underrepresented and marginalized communities.
At GWI, you will find a place where you can contribute meaningfully, grow professionally, and belong fully.

Drive rapid response to customer-critical incidents by diagnosing, triaging, and resolving complex production issues that span multiple services across the Agent Platform.
Lead systematic root-cause analysis and translate incident learnings into durable reliability, scalability, observability, and operability improvements.
Quickly build a systems-level understanding of unfamiliar services and codebases, collaborating closely with engineering teams to resolve complex cross-service issues.

We provide engineers with modern AI-powered tools to improve both engineering productivity and software quality.

Support data security and governance work (e.g., PII masking, access controls) and contribute to data delivery work, including reverse ETL integrations

Empower every employee.
At Flip, we have a clear goal: to revolutionize the world for frontline workers and give them a voice. Become a Flip Game Changer and work with an unbeatable team to ensure that all employees, no matter where they work, have access to their company's internal information. If you're ready to make an impact and shape the work lives of millions of people, then you've come to the right place!
Our Mission: Connect every employee to everything they need in one touch.
Job Description
Flip is the frontline employee experience platform. Hundreds of thousands of people who do not work at a desk open Flip to reach everything their employer's digital world holds for them and Bosch, REWE and Porsche are a a few of the companies that run it. The hard part is the last mile into a decades-old enterprise IT landscape, and that last mile is this role.
As a Customer Engineer you sit on the edge of the product, inside the customer's environment: their identity stack, their HR systems, their security review, their AI roadmap.

You take a Flip tenant from nothing to hundreds of thousands of live users and you decide how the technical side gets solved, sometimes by designing the integration and enabling the customer's IT to build it, sometimes by building the first version yourself and handing it over.

That includes where our AI goes live: agents in the frontline app, tool access over MCP, and the authentication questions underneath them that nobody has solved yet.
What you can expect
Technical ownership end to end: You own the technical side of enterprise onboardings, from the first architecture conversation to a stable live rollout at scale.
Integrations that make Flip load-bearing: You design and land identity and authentication (OIDC, Entra ID, Frontline Identity), user provisioning (SCIM), REST APIs and connections into HR and ops systems such as SAP SuccessFactors, Workday or UKG.
Advise and enable instead of absorb: You bring the customer's IT, their partners and our external development partners to a solution you would sign off on, and you make sure they can run it without you.
Build where building unblocks: Where building is the fastest way to prove an approach or to unblock a rollout, you build the first version and then hand it over cleanly, with the documentation and the handover conversation that make it stick.
AI where it meets the customer: You lead how agents, MCP-based tool access and agent-to-agent scenarios land at enterprise customers, including the auth and data boundaries that have to hold around them.
Technical authority in the account: You work with customer project management, IT, security, functional departments and works councils, you decide the technical questions, and you feed the gaps you see back into our product and engineering teams. Expect regular travel to customer sites, roughly 10 to 30 percent of your time.

s.h: What you bring to the table
s.t:
Must-haves
Around 3 to 5 (or more) years in IT or tech consulting, customer engineering, forward deployed engineering, solutions engineering or SaaS implementation, with real enterprise exposure.
Hands-on experience with enterprise integration and identity: SSO and authentication (OIDC, OAuth, Entra ID or comparable), REST APIs and API-based integrations delivered inside real enterprise IT environments.
Customer-facing technical responsibility in enterprise projects, where you made the technical calls together with IT, security and functional departments rather than only coordinating them.
Genuine technical depth without being a full-time production developer: you read code, review a design, debug an integration and build a working prototype.
German at C1 level or above and fluent English.
Nice-to-haves
Provisioning experience (SCIM) and integrations into HR or workforce systems such as SAP SuccessFactors, Workday or UKG.
An informed, current view on where agentic AI is heading: MCP, A2A, EMA and the authentication questions underneath them. We are looking for someone who follows the field closely and has an opinion, not for years of experience that cannot exist yet.
Prior work as a Customer Engineer or Forward Deployed Engineer at a product company, rather than in classic consulting only.
Workflow automation tooling (n8n or similar), comfort with logs, metrics and dashboards, or experience with German co-determination and enterprise data protection.

Work mode: We’re remote-first, giving you flexibility to work from home. At the same time, we deeply value the power of in-person collaboration. Depending on the role, you’ll join occasional team events, workshops, or meetings in our Berlin or Stuttgart offices - always with plenty of notice. The exact balance will be discussed during your interview.
Work-Life-Balance: We don't want you to grow roots to your desk chair. That's why we cover the costs of your E-Gym-Wellpass membership and offer job bike leasing.
Celebrating success: Expect highly motivated and committed people in a relaxed working atmosphere.
Be part of something bigger : You actively shape Flip in your role. Along the way, you are an enabler of the rapid growth process of a young tech company and grow towards your goals, fun is guaranteed.
Happy to be a Flipster: Stay tuned for regular team events and culture days that bring us together as Flipsters.
Working abroad: At Flip you can also work abroad in the European Union. Let's talk about remote work in the interview.
At Flip, everyone is welcome - no matter what gender you identify as or how old you are. Sexual identity , origin, religion, world view and disabilities do not influence your potential job at Flip. The most important thing is that YOU fit in!

Humboldt is a subteam of Flex Trading Enablement (Trading Optimisation). We sit at the intersection of commercial energy trading and the green transition, and we own Asset Backed Trading.
Asset Backed Trading went live in March 2026. It already runs in two countries, with more markets and features on the way. There is a lot of room to shape how it is built.
It models trading, ancillary service allocation, and dispatch for EU portfolios of batteries, solar and wind. We take market and position updates from Flex APIs, allocate energy and services that help stabilise the grid such as FCR and aFRR across the portfolio, and disaggregate those decisions to individual sites. We can both help traders make decisions about how to trade, and disaggregate said trades into per-asset dispatch decisions.
This is production software with genuine commercial and operational impact. It not only support key traders' workflows, but also it drives physical asset dispatch and the delivery of grid services, so we care a lot about getting it right. You will work with data scientists and traders to turn prototypes into reliable, well tested services they can trust.

We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join Humboldt and help shape Asset Backed Trading as it grows into new countries and capabilities.
You will work in a Python monorepo of serverless services: event driven pipelines that ingest market and asset data, build optimisation problems, call solvers, and write dispatch and trading positions back out. You will also help evolve the interfaces with other Flex services and APIs that Asset Backed Trading depends on.

HOW you will contribute to the company as a Software Engineer
As a Software Engineer, you would will be part of a 400+ people Tech organisation. Each engineer is part of a squad focussing on a part of the product, reporting to a Team Lead or an Engineering Manager.
Each squad is made with all the skills needed to build features end to end in autonomy, you will be working daily with a product manager, a designer and software engineers.
As a Software Engineer you will take part of the discovery phase of the projects with the Product Manager and Designer to define the feature to build; then you will participate with other engineers to design the software architecture, build it, test it and release it to production.
The squad is also working on supporting customers using the features built by monitoring and fixing issues in production.

As a Software Engineer on the AWS Emulator team, you’ll help expand and harden LocalStack ’s AWS emulator by taking ownership of individual services and making them behave as closely as possible to real AWS.
The challenge is genuinely unusual: you’ll reimplement cloud services that you can only observe from the outside. Making a service “work” is one thing; matching AWS behaviour — including edge cases and undocumented details — is a very different engineering problem.
We’re looking for someone who learns quickly, enjoys tackling unfamiliar problems, and can turn incomplete information into working solutions. You’ll have end-to-end ownership of your services, from investigating how they behave and deciding what needs to be built through implementation, testing, and ongoing improvements.
AI is a core part of how the team works. You’ll use modern AI coding and agentic tools to make development more efficient while maintaining the quality and reliability expected by LocalStack users. The role offers a clear path to broader service ownership and technical leadership as your scope grows.
✅ What you will be working on/responsible for
Internalize services off moto. Independently take AWS services from moto-backed to fully first-party implementations, owning store design for persistence, full API operation coverage, and conformance to LocalStack conventions rather than transplanted moto code. Measured by services shipped and their size.
Close parity gaps in owned services. Raise snapshot-test coverage against real AWS for the documented API surface for owned services, with a measurable reduction in parity defects reported from the field.
Own services end-to-end after they ship. Act as first responder for their services: customer-reported parity bugs triaged and turned around within 5 days median, including those that surface through Terraform and CDK rather than direct API calls.
Raise the team's testing floor. Contribute reusable test infrastructure (conformance harnesses, snapshot tooling, fixtures) that other engineers adopt for services they do not own.
Grow visibly in scope. By month 12, be trusted to scope and sequence an internalization independently, from API-documentation analysis through to shipped provider, without needing the plan handed to them.

A strong testing mindset — you use tests as a tool for understanding and designing systems, not just for checking finished code.
Hands-on experience with AI coding and agentic development tools. We’re looking for more than basic Copilot usage: you should have used these tools substantially to build and ship real software and understand both their strengths and limitations.
Fast learning and strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to quickly understand unfamiliar systems and work effectively with incomplete information.

Who We Are
DoiT is a global technology company that works with cloud-driven organizations to leverage the cloud to drive business growth and innovation. We combine data, technology, and human expertise to ensure our customers operate in a well-architected and scalable state - from planning to production.

The Opportunity
Cloud spend is no longer just AWS, Google Cloud and Azure. Our customers now run a large and growing share of their technology spend through SaaS platforms, data clouds and AI vendors - and every one of those vendors is an integration that brings another slice of their spend into view.
You'll own DoiT's Integrations Framework and the experience built on top of it. You'll work AI-augmented from day one. Integration development is spec-driven work against constantly changing third-party APIs: one of the highest-leverage places to apply agentic AI tooling. Building new integrations. This is the core of the role. Working AI-augmented. Push on what agentic tooling can do for this codebase, and bring judgement about where AI raises velocity and where a human still has to hold the quality bar.
Integration management experience. Build the interfaces customers use to connect, configure and trust their integrations: health and status visibility, actionable error states, credential and key rotation, and clear feedback when something needs attention.
Self-service by default. Design self-service into the framework from the start - backfills, reconnects and diagnostics that customers and internal teams run themselves.
API-first. Build capabilities so they're fully available through APIs, not just the UI. Both humans and agents should be able to drive the platform.
Implementing features end-to-end. From proposal, through spec and implementation, to maintenance. You're expected to propose things you think would be a good addition, not wait for a spec.
